gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the factory 8-inch rear screen costs: it only comes on the Premium trims, so the cheapest way to get it from Tesla is the $6,000 MSRP step from Standard RWD ($39,990) to Premium RWD ($45,990), or $8,000 from Standard AWD ($41,990) to Premium AWD ($49,990).
standout_why: I could not open any tesla.com page; all three cited ones returned HTTP 403 to my fetcher. ChatGPT's answer, drawn from tesla.com/modely, the 'Introducing New Model Y' page and the Touchscreen manual page, says only that 'some Standard versions do not' have the rear screen, with no price. The ManualsLib copy of the manual (result 16) lists the screen's functions but gives no size, trim or price. The Not a Tesla App article (result 18, 2026-06-05) covers only the 16-inch front screen and the base prices; it never mentions the rear screen. None of these pages turns the trim gap into a cost for the rear screen.
decides: For a new-car buyer who mainly wants a back-seat screen, the factory route costs at least $6,000 (RWD) or $8,000 (AWD), and that money also buys the glass roof, the other Premium features and more range. For a buyer of a Standard car, or an owner of one, this points to an add-on rear console screen built for the Juniper Standard, such as the Hansshow H86. Its last listed price of $399.99 is about 6.7% of the $6,000 step ($399.99 / $6,000), but I could not reopen it today (HTTP 429), so the price needs checking before publishing. One more point: Motor1 reports the Standard has no rear seat heaters, so any 'seat heat control' an add-on screen promises does nothing on a Standard.

findings.label: What the factory rear screen controls
findings.value: Rear climate on/off, rear fan speed, rear seat heaters, front passenger seat fore/aft, media, video streaming, gaming, up to 2 Bluetooth headphones, volume, air-flow preset; can be locked from the front (Controls > Display > Lock Rear Display)
